_notes: Game money the balance tool needs that the mod's data files don't hold. price = Item.DefaultMarketPrice, wholesale = Item.wholesalePrice (before the import price index and the difficulty's market multiplier, both 1.0 here), box = units per wholesale box: Big Copilot's ba_store_rules.json, validated against saves. The hot dog's $11.65 was also seen in game (Milestone 1). priceIndex = each neighbourhood's average price index, the most every customer there pays relative to the reference price (Big Copilot's openStore facts; opener research of 23 Sep 2026). equipment = default item prices from Big Copilot's ba_item_prices.json; the coffee machine is the industrial one ($4,700): the cheap one ($400) is office equipment (ItemType 0x8000), not shop equipment. Kabob, popcorn, cotton candy and slushi (cinema concessions) added 9 October 2026 for the new-foods study; equipment keys industrialgrill, industrialfryer, concessionsdisplaycase and slushimachine are the vanilla items' prices, for the proposed grill, fryer, concessions and slushie pieces.
_market: The game's market demand (0 to 100) for the cinema items in the four neighbourhoods it keeps it for: 100 - providers x 100 / 7, at least about 31 (ProductMarketHelper.CalculateDemand), counting cinemas (and theatres, for popcorn) as providers. Used instead of --market there.
_marketLimits: Items the game keeps market demand for only in these neighbourhoods (Item.limitDemandToNeighbourhoods, ba_store_rules.json). Elsewhere the calculator uses 100, as Core does when the adapter leaves them out.
